newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin resumes presidential powers after 23 hours.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin resumes presidential powers after 23 hours.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday reclaimed control of Russia's nuclear arsenal and other presidential powers which he had transferred to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin for the period of his heart operation.

Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, said by telephone from his Kremlin office that Yeltsin signed the decree at 6 a.m. (0300 GMT), or 23 hours after he had delegated his authority to Chernomyrdin and gone under the surgeon's knife.
"He woke up and signed the decree," he said.
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin felt better than his doctors had expected. "He surprises doctors with his good state. He feels quite well for this stage," he said.
Doctors said earlier that Yeltsin's seven-hour operation included five bypasses.
The doctors who operated on Yeltsin were due to meet at 9 a.m. (0600 GMT) to review his progress.
Yeltsin, 65, recovered consciousness on Tuesday evening after the quintuple bypass operation, which lasted seven hours.
It was not clear whether he was still breathing through a lung ventilator.
